title: The pressure of ministry
scripture_text: “I am sending you out like sheep among wolves. Therefore be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves. Be on your guard; you will be handed over to the local councils and be flogged in the synagogues. On my account you will be brought before governors and kings as witnesses to them and to the Gentiles. But when they arrest you, do not worry about what to say or how to say it. At that time you will be given what to say, for it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you “Brother will betray brother to death, and a father his child; children will rebel against their parents and have them put to death. You will be hated by everyone because of me, but the one who stands firm to the end will be saved. When you are persecuted in one place, flee to another. Truly I tell you, you will not finish going through the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes. The student is not above the teacher, nor a servant above his master. It is enough for students to be like their teachers, and servants like their masters. If the head of the house has been called Beelzebul, how much more the members of his household! So do not be afraid of them, for there is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, or hidden that will not be made known. What I tell you in the dark, speak in the daylight; what is whispered in your ear, proclaim from the roofs. Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Rather, be afraid of the One who can destroy both soul and body in hell. Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? Yet not one of them will fall to the ground outside your Father’s care. And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. So don’t be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows. “Whoever acknowledges me before others, I will also acknowledge before my Father in heaven. But whoever disowns me before others, I will disown before my Father in heaven. Do not suppose that I have come to bring peace to the earth. I did not come to bring peace, but a sword. For I have come to turn a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law—a man’s enemies will be the members of his own household. Anyone who loves their father or mother more than me is not worthy of me; anyone who loves their son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me. Whoever does not take up their cross and follow me is not worthy of me. Whoever finds their life will lose it, and whoever loses their life for my sake will find it. Anyone who welcomes you welcomes me, and anyone who welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me. Whoever welcomes a prophet as a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward, and whoever welcomes a righteous person as a righteous person will receive a righteous person’s reward. And if anyone gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones who is my disciple, truly I tell you, that person will certainly not lose their reward.”
devotional:
In the first 15 verses Jesus gives us the principles for ministry. The rest of the chapter Jesus talks about the pressure of ministry. Matthew 10:16-42

Jesus spends more time in talking about the stress, strain, and pressure of ministry than he does about the success or achievements of ministry.

Why is that?

How we handle the pressure and pain of ministry will be a more authentic indication of our spirituality than a successful ministry would be.

Jesus is more concerned about those who are doing the work than the work they are doing, so he has more to say about how they handle themselves under pressure than he has to say about what they are doing.

In this passage Jesus says more about inner attitude that he does about practical steps we could take to avoid the pressure of ministry. Look at some of the attitudes Jesus encourages.

A. Be Shrewd 16a

B. Be innocent 16b.

C. Be on your guard 17a.

D. Do not worry 19a.

E. Be humble like Jesus 24 – 25

F. Do not be afraid 26a.

G. Do not be afraid of those who kill the body 28a.

H. Fear Him (God) who destroys both body and soul in hell 28b.

I. Do not be afraid, for you are valuable 31.

J. Love Jesus above all 37.

K. Loose your life 39.

So how we react to the pressure of ministry has nothing to do with the source or nature of specific pressure, but more to do with what is, (or what is not in) our hearts.

It is important to notice what Jesus did not tell these disciples what to do when they were under pressure. He did not say remember your call, remember what I have called you to. Often people use the call of God upon their lives as a means of being faithful and persistent. I have often heard it said that when things get tough, you recall the time God called you and this will keep you going. On the surface this sounds spiritual and even helpful. But if we were to consider this philosophy a bit deeper, you will discover that it is both dangerous and unhelpful.

Spiritual experience of the past (the call) will never see a person through the crisis of the present. The only way a person can cope with the pressure of the present is to develop their relationship with God in the here and now. What God is saying to you in the present, what God is doing in your life now, is more important than any ‘call’ you may have had in the past.

The power of being wise and innocent.

Jesus continues Matthew 10:16 ‘I am sending you out like sheep among wolves. Therefore be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves. This would have been a good place, to divide the text, and I think the tone of Jesus voice may have changed here. Matthew 10:16 in the AV reads “Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.” The word Behold is not in the NIV text, but it is a very important word, and it helps us understand what is happening here. The Greek word is KAI IDOU “and behold.”

The word Behold in Matthew, is a “Flag” word. It is a word that he uses when something unexpected or out of the ordinary is going to happen, something surprising or new, see Matthew 1:20 12:2.

So what Jesus says here is totally unexpected. Here Jesus is introducing something that is completely unexpected and somewhat shocking. Jesus was sending unexpected people to have an unexpected ministry. This adds to their vulnerability. Who wants to be sheep amongst wolves?
prayer: Father it is only my relationship with you in the present that will sustain me in ministry.
